newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to watch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to watch.

text.p: * Viacom Inc is expected to report a fourth quarter loss per share of $0.13 compared to a loss of $0.07 a year ago, according to First Call. The stock closed at 34-7/8.

* Schlumberger Ltd was off 1/2 at 100-1/8 in London while Baker Hughes Inc was down 3/8 at at 35-1/8. The weekly financial newspaper Barron's said falling oil and natural gas prices had aborted the rally in energy shares.
* EIS International Inc said it would restructure and reorganize and focus on its core Call Center business. The stock closed at 5-7/8.

* The multiple of about twice its growth rate that Coca-Cola Co has gained is "extravagant" according to a columnist for the weekly financial newspaper Barron's. Alan Abelson wrote in his column "Up & Down Wall Street" that Coke's stock over the past year has gone from under 40 to above 63 and closed Friday at 61. "It thus is selling at 40 times the latest 12-month earnings and around 37 time this year's estimate, both historic highs," Abelson wrote.
Coke was fell 3/8 to 60-5/8 in London.

U.S. television network CBS Corp, a unit of Westinghouse Electric Corp , expects to raise enough money for a winning bid for the broadcast rights to professional football as part of its efforts to raise ratings, according to Barron's.

The paper said in its March 3 edition CBS expected to get cash from two recently acquired cable outlets to acquire the rights to show games of the National Football League. Westinghouse shares closed at 17-3/8. Westinghouse closed at 17-3/8.

* Philip Morris Cos Inc was boosted by news it had won access to the names of 400,000 Florida Medicaid patients to help its challenge to the financial claims of the state of Florida. The state is suing tobacco companies for more than a billion dollars in Healthcare costs associated with smoking-related sickness. Shares were up 1/4 at 135-3/8.

* CSX Corp and Conrail Inc are close to a pact that would boost the price for Conrail by $1 billion to $10.5 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported in its Monday electronic edition. CSX closed at 46-1/8. Conrail closed at 104-1/2.
